\begin{lemma}[Gaussian CDF sublevel measure]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measureReal_standardGaussianCDF_le}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measureReal_standardGaussianCDF_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianCDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianCDF_lt_one, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianCDF_pos, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianCDF_quantile, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianCDF_strictMono, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianQuantile}

For every $a\in[0,1]$, the standard Gaussian measure of $\{t\in\mathbb R:\Phi(t)\le a\}$
is $a$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Uniformity of the Gaussian CDF transform]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measureReal_standardGaussianCDF_comp_le}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measureReal_standardGaussianCDF_comp_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measureReal_standardGaussianCDF_le, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.continuous_standardGaussianCDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianCDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a measurable space, let $\mu$ be a measure on $\Omega$, and let
$X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be measure-preserving from $\mu$ to the standard Gaussian
measure. For every $a\in[0,1]$, the real measure of
$\{\omega\in\Omega:\Phi(X(\omega))\le a\}$ is $a$, where $\Phi$ is the standard Gaussian
cumulative distribution function.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian CDF band measure bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measureReal_standardGaussianCDF_inter_sub_le}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measureReal_standardGaussianCDF_inter_sub_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measureReal_standardGaussianCDF_comp_le, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.continuous_standardGaussianCDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianCDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{4}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a finite measure space, and let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ push $\mu$
forward to the standard Gaussian probability measure. For any measurable set
$A\subseteq\Omega$ and $a,b\in[0,1]$ with $a\le b$, the difference between the measures
of $A\cap\{\omega:\Phi(X(\omega))\le b\}$ and $A\cap\{\omega:\Phi(X(\omega))\le a\}$ is
at most $b-a$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian CDF threshold measure stability]

\difficulty{4}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a finite measure space, let $X\colon\Omega\to\mathbb R$ have the
standard Gaussian distribution under $\mu$, and let $A\subseteq\Omega$. For
$a,b\in[0,1]$, the absolute difference between the measures of
$A\cap\{\omega:\Phi(X(\omega))\le a\}$ and $A\cap\{\omega:\Phi(X(\omega))\le b\}$ is at
most $|a-b|$, where $\Phi$ is the standard Gaussian distribution function.
\end{lemma}

Gaussian variables $X,Y$, the probability that $X\le s$ and $\rho
X+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,Y\le t$ equals
$\displaystyle\int_{(-\infty,s]}\Phi\!\left(\frac{t-\rho
x}{\sqrt{1-\rho^2}}\right)\,d\gamma(x)$, where $\gamma$ is standard Gaussian measure and
$\Phi$ its distribution function.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Lipschitz continuity of Gaussian bivariate stability]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lipschitzOnWith_gaussianBivariateStability}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lipschitzOnWith_gaussianBivariateStability}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_gaussianBivariateStability_sub_le, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianBivariateStability}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\rho\in[-1,1]$. On the square $[0,1]^2$, the function sending $(\alpha,\beta)$ to
the Gaussian probability of the event that a standard Gaussian variable $Z$ satisfies
$\Phi(Z)\le\alpha$ and $\Phi(\rho Z+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}W)\le\beta$, with $W$ an independent
standard Gaussian variable, is Lipschitz with constant $2$ for the product metric.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Continuity of Gaussian bivariate stability]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.continuousOn_gaussianBivariateStability}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.continuousOn_gaussianBivariateStability}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianBivariateStability, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lipschitzOnWith_gaussianBivariateStability}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\rho\in[-1,1]$. For independent standard Gaussian random variables $X,Y$, define
$S_\rho(\alpha,\beta)=\mathbb P\bigl(\Phi(X)\le\alpha,\ \Phi(\rho
X+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,Y)\le\beta\bigr)$, where $\Phi$ is the standard Gaussian distribution
function. Then $S_\rho$ is continuous on $[0,1]^2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Measurability of composed Gaussian stability]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurable_gaussianBivariateStability_comp}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurable_gaussianBivariateStability_comp}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.continuousOn_gaussianBivariateStability, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianBivariateStability}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\Omega$ be a measurable space, let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and let $f,g:\Omega\to\mathbb
R$ be measurable functions taking values in $[0,1]$. Then $x\mapsto G_\rho(f(x),g(x))$
is measurable, where $G_\rho(\alpha,\beta)$ is the probability that a pair $(Z,\rho
Z+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,W)$ has respective standard Gaussian distribution-function values at
most $\alpha$ and $\beta$, with $Z,W$ independent standard Gaussian random variables.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Integrability of composed Gaussian bivariate stability]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_gaussianBivariateStability_comp}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_gaussianBivariateStability_comp}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianBivariateStability, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianBivariateStability_mem_unitInterval, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurable_gaussianBivariateStability_comp}
\difficulty{3}
Let $(\Omega,\mathcal A)$ be a measurable space with a finite measure $\mu$, let
$\rho\in[-1,1]$, and let $\Phi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function. For
$a,b\in\mathbb R$, define $B(\rho,a,b)$ as the probability that $U\le a$ and $\rho
U+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}V\le b$, where $U,V$ are independent standard Gaussian variables. If
$f,g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ are measurable and take values in $[0,1]$, then $x\mapsto
B(\rho,f(x),g(x))$ is integrable with respect to $\mu$.
\end{lemma}
